Student Internship Selection Prediction using Logistic Regression¶

Problem Statement¶

The internship selection process can involve multiple student-related factors that may influence the final selection outcome. Analyzing these factors manually can be time-consuming.

This project aims to use Machine Learning to predict internship selection outcomes and demonstrate how Logistic Regression can be applied to a binary classification problem.

Target Variable Analysis¶

The target variable is Internship_Selected, which represents the internship selection status of a student.

It is a binary variable with two possible outcomes:

  • 0 → Student was not selected
  • 1 → Student was selected

In this section, we examine the distribution of the two classes to understand whether the target variable is balanced or imbalanced.

Data Cleaning¶

Handling Missing Values¶

In [25]:
# Separate numerical and categorical columns
numerical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=np.number).columns
categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include="object").columns

# Fill numerical missing values with median
for column in numerical_cols:
    df[column] = df[column].fillna(df[column].median())

# Fill categorical missing values with mode
for column in categorical_cols:
    df[column] = df[column].fillna(df[column].mode()[0])

# Check missing values again
df.isnull().sum()

# Detect outliers using IQR method

Q1 = df[numerical_columns].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = df[numerical_columns].quantile(0.75)

IQR = Q3 - Q1

outliers = ((df[numerical_columns] < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR)) |
            (df[numerical_columns] > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)))

outliers.sum()

from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

    ('model', LogisticRegression(random_state=42))
])

ROC-AUC / ROC Curve¶

The model achieved a ROC-AUC score of 0.815, indicating a good ability to distinguish between Selected and Not Selected students.

In [60]:
from sklearn.metrics import roc_curve, roc_auc_score
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Calculate prediction probabilities
y_prob = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

# Calculate ROC curve
fpr, tpr, thresholds = roc_curve(y_test, y_prob)

# Calculate AUC
auc_score = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob)

print("ROC-AUC Score:", auc_score)

# Plot ROC Curve
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
plt.plot(fpr, tpr, label=f"AUC = {auc_score:.2f}")
plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], linestyle="--")
plt.xlabel("False Positive Rate")
plt.ylabel("True Positive Rate")
plt.title("ROC Curve")
plt.legend()
plt.show()

ROC-AUC Score: 0.7535041306971131

Model Performance Results¶

The model achieved 71.19% accuracy. The Precision, Recall, and F1 Score are approximately 67.91%, 68.42%, and 68.16%, respectively. The ROC-AUC score of 0.75 indicates a good ability to distinguish between Selected and Not Selected students.

Conclusion¶

In this project, Exploratory Data Analysis, Data Cleaning, and Data Preprocessing were performed on the student internship dataset. The categorical features were encoded, the data was divided into training and testing sets, and feature scaling was applied.

A Logistic Regression model was trained to predict whether a student would be selected for an internship. The model was evaluated using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 Score, and ROC-AUC Score.

The evaluation results provide an overall understanding of the model's classification performance and its ability to predict internship selection outcomes.

Future Scope¶

The project can be further improved by using a larger and more diverse dataset containing additional student-related features. Other classification algorithms such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine can also be tested and compared with Logistic Regression.

Hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation can be applied to improve model performance. The project can also be developed into a simple application that predicts internship selection based on student details.
